set.body:
Raised at the moment Epic 9 was claimed, so it can be fixed before the report is written rather than after.

Epic 9 acceptance: "Print/format/coercion methods and runnable Rd examples cover the first user journey."

Print/format/coercion is DONE and verified - 26 S3method entries where my first review counted zero, and as_neurovol() round-trips exactly. No issue there.

Rd examples are the gap. 82 Rd files, 5 with \examples, and they are the newest surface rather than the first journey:

  HAS examples: crossnobis.Rd, plan_crossnobis.Rd, plan_geometry.Rd, neural_metric.Rd, metric_components.Rd

The first user journey, as the README itself presents it, is

  relation() -> compile_frame(searchlights()) -> geometry() -> contrast() / rdm() / rsa()

and then out via as_neurovol(). Checked individually:

  geometry           no examples
  relation           no examples
  rdm                no examples
  rsa                no examples
  contrast           no examples
  compile_frame      no examples
  searchlights       no examples
  lm_relation_fit    no examples
  as_neurovol        no examples

So the five that exist document the Epic 5-7 metric/plan family, which is the most recently written surface and the least likely to be a reader first stop. The criterion as worded is not met.

This is a small amount of work - the README already contains a complete runnable sequence for exactly these functions, so the examples can be lifted from prose that is known to execute.

ONE INTERACTION WORTH PLANNING FOR: Rd examples are executed by R CMD check. Adding nine of them enlarges the check surface at the same moment bd-01KZY1YJ426SEKJM6Q4THDAR7J asks for a check that has not been run in 10708 lines. Better to add the examples first and then run the check once, than to certify a check and then add executable examples to it.

Credit where due, both verified this pass: the README now opens with the fMRI problem ("estimate where experimental effects are reproducible, how their multivariate geometry changes across the brain, and which local patterns generalize across independent runs"), which addresses the opening I criticised in the first review. And the two package-free contract files that tested oracle-against-oracle are gone, while the independent oracle helpers survive - helper-effect-form-laws.R, helper-evidence-pairing-laws.R, helper-measurement-form-oracle.R, plus a new helper-residual-statistics.R. That is the resolution I asked for.
set.title: Epic 9 criterion: Rd examples cover the newest surface, not the first user journey (5 of 82)
